facts.statement: Trialestes was an extinct genus of crocodylomorphs that lived during the Late Triassic in South America.
facts.quote: Trialestes is an extinct genus of Late Triassic (Carnian) crocodylomorphs that lived in South America.

facts.statement: Trialestes was once classified as a dinosaur because it was adapted as a terrestrial, running carnivore.
facts.quote: It has been classified as a dinosaur in the past due it being adapted as a terrestrial, running carnivore.

facts.statement: Trialestes is classified within Sphenosuchia, a group of early crocodylomorph relatives of modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: It is classified in Sphenosuchia, which were early relatives of crocodylians.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PVL 2561 was found in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: the holotype specimen PVL 2561, found in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina

facts.statement: The type species Trialestes romeri was named in 1963.
facts.quote: The type species, T. romeri, was named in 1963.

facts.statement: Researchers Irmis, Nesbitt, and Sues (2013) noted that some material previously referred to Trialestes actually belongs to dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Irmis, Nesbitt and Sues (2013) noted that some of the material referred to this taxon is actually dinosaurian

facts.statement: The holotype specimen preserves unambiguous crocodylomorph traits, confirming it is not a dinosaur.
facts.quote: comprises a single individual that preserves unambiguous crocodylomorph synapomorphies

facts.statement: Trialestes lived during the Carnian stage of the Triassic, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)
